subject: Performance SLO p95/p99 - Hosted vs current provider - postcall recap
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@finlytics.com>, Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO p95/p99 - Hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Thanks again for taking time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a focused perf qualification: 

Summary of what you shared (please correct if I misstate):
- Current provider (managed endpoints): end-to-end p95 ~420 ms, p99 ~950 ms (Q2 latency samples)
- Typical peak throughput: ~200 QPS sustained, short spikes up to ~450 QPS
- Concurrent connections: ~50-60 during peak business hours
- Streaming is a hard requirement for some UIs (need first chunk within ~100-200ms for progressive render)
- Average request size: ~120 tokens output, prompt ~60 tokens (varies by feature)

Redwood's asks / clarifying items we need to run a meaningful comparison:
1) Can you share the raw latency sample report or a small anonymized log (p95/p99 per 1-minute window) — I attached a sample template (finlytics_latency_report_q2.pdf) that would help standardize.
2) Please confirm the traffic shape for the most critical route (QPS distribution, typical concurrency by minute).
3) Is end-to-end latency measured client-side (includes network + render) or server-side only?

What Redwood can offer for the qualification:
- We can run a hosted API baseline test across your traffic shape and deliver p95/p99 projections and the actual test run metrics.
- Initial expectation (rough, depends on exact traffic and token mix): hosted API p95 ~160-220 ms, p99 ~280-420 ms under comparable throughput with streaming enabled.
- We'll propose a 2-week proof-of-concept (POC) with a controlled load test followed by a short production pilot to validate end-to-end metrics.

Next steps I propose:
- Tara/Mike: share the latency sample + one week of production traffic histogram (anonymized) by EOD Thu 6/30
- Redwood (Marissa/Aditya): prepare test harness + estimated infra for a 2-week POC by Fri 7/2
- Quick sync early next week to align on exact test plan (I can host)

Attaching our summary spreadsheet (redwood_perf_summary.xlsx) with the test template and a sample measurement rubric.

Thanks — laura

--
Laura Bennett

From: Tara Singh <tara@finlytics.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO p95/p99 - Hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Thanks Laura — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and I'm attaching the Q2 sample report you asked for (finlytics_latency_report_q2.pdf).

Clarifications from our side:
- The p95/p99 numbers I quoted are client-side (measured in our web app, so they include some client render and network times). Server-side medians are lower but the client numbers are what our SLAs track.
- Peak sustained throughput is ~200 QPS during business hours; we see hourly spikes that can reach 400–450 QPS for ~1–5 minute bursts when we release marketing emails.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrent requests is 40–60; during spikes we’ve seen that hit ~80 for short windows.
- Streaming is mandatory for our interactive assistant feature — we need the first token/chunk to arrive within ~150ms to keep UX snappy. Full-stream completion can be slower.

I'm attaching the Q2 latency report (anonymized): finlytics_latency_report_q2.pdf — it has per-route histograms and a minute-level time series that should be useful. I'll also work with our infra team to export a 24‑hour production traffic snapshot (timestamps and per-minute QPS).

Targets we need Redwood to validate for us:
- End-to-end p95 <= 350 ms
- End-to-end p99 <= 900 ms
- Support streaming with first-chunk latency <= 150 ms under expected concurrency

We'll aim to get the 24h snapshot to you by Thu 6/30. Let us know if you need anything else to scope the POC.

Thanks,
Tara

--
Tara Singh
Head of Platform\FinLytics
tara@finlytics.com

Attachment: finlytics_latency_report_q2.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO p95/p99 - Hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Perfect — thanks for the report and the concrete targets, Tara. A few quick notes based on what you shared:

1) Measurement alignment: since your SLA is client-side, our POC will include an end-to-end measurement (client-like) to match your numbers. We'll instrument both server-side and client-proxy measurements so we can separate network/render from server processing.

2) Streaming: we'll validate first-chunk latency under concurrency in the POC. If your first-chunk requirement is <=150ms, we'll include a focused streaming benchmark for that path.

3) POC plan (high level):
   - Day 0–2: ingest your 24h traffic snapshot and parameterize the harness (token mix, route weights, arrival distribution)
   - Day 3–7: hosted baseline runs (multiple windows) to measure p95/p99 and streaming first-chunk latency
   - Day 8–14: optional pilot with a small % of production traffic (controlled) to validate end-to-end in the wild

I've asked Aditya to size the infra and propose an estimate for the hosted test runs. Marissa will own the POC coordination and reporting back to FinLytics.

We'll keep the report concise and include both server-only and client-like end-to-end metrics so you can see where time is being spent.

Talk soon — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference

- I'll set up the shared dashboard for measurements and a short results template we can hand to Tara once tests complete.
- Proposed kickoff: Mon 7/5 for Day 0 (ingest snapshot). We can move earlier if FinLytics delivers the traffic snapshot before Thu.

Cost note for the POC (ballpark): $6k–$12k depending on whether we need Dedicated capacity for peak concurrency windows — I'll include options in the sizing doc.
